literal: Of the desert path, the vākai tree's dense clusters of white dry pods, / like the pebbles of a sounding anklet, their grains making sound, / as the west wind shakes them in the forest, / we shall go, my friend, our lover has bestowed grace on us.
translation: My friend, our lover has shown us his grace. We shall now go through the forest where the west wind shakes the dense clusters of white, dry pods of the vākai trees on the desert path, making their seeds rattle like the pebbles inside a sounding anklet.
modern: தோழியே! நம் தலைவர் நமக்கு அருள் புரிந்துள்ளார். பாலைவனப் பாதையில் உள்ள வாகை மரத்தின் அடர்ந்த வெண்மையான உலர்ந்த நெற்றுகள், உள்ளே இருக்கும் விதைகள் ஒலிக்கும் சிலம்பின் பரல் போல ஒலிக்குமாறு, கோடைக்காற்று அசைக்கும் காட்டின் வழியே நாம் செல்வோம்.
explanation: The speaker is the companion (thozhi) addressing the heroine (thalaivi). The hero, who had left to earn wealth through the difficult desert paths (pālai), has returned, having accomplished his task and bestowed his grace upon them. The companion joyfully tells the heroine that they will now travel together through the forest. She describes the desert landscape where the dry, white pods of the vākai tree are shaken by the hot west wind (kōdai), making a rattling sound like the pebbles inside a dancer's anklet. This vivid auditory image of the dry pods rattling in the wind beautifully contrasts the harshness of the desert with the joy of the hero's return, marking the transition from separation to union.
